LOS ANGELES, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP ("SBS"), a national shareholder rights litigation firm, announces that it is investigating claims on behalf of investors of Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. ("Applied Aerospace" or "the Company") (NYSE: AADX) for violations of the securities laws.

INVESTIGATION DETAILS: The investigation focuses on whether the Company issued false and/or misleading statements and/or failed to disclose information pertinent to investors. Applied Aerospace failed to inform investors of constraints on supply for specialized components. The Company misled shareholders about delays in approval for the overhaul program for Apache helicopter rotor heads, which led to delays in revenue recognition. The Company suffered harsh ramp costs that impacted its gross profit margin. Based on these facts, shares of Applied Aerospace fell sharply.

data.title: ABB to Buy Germany's Ziehl-Abegg for $2.22 Billion
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

ABB said it agreed to buy Ziehl-Abegg, a German manufacturer of fans, motors and ventilation systems, for $2.22 billion.

The Swiss engineering group said Monday that the deal expands its offering for heating, ventilation and air conditioning as well as industrial-cooling applications.

Ziehl-Abegg is expected to generate about $1.4 billion in revenue in 2026 and its products are used in HVAC, data centers, clean rooms, medical technology and elevator drives, among other uses.

The acquisition aims to add electronically commutated fans to the portfolio of motors and drives of ABB's Motion business, the company said. ABB said Ziehl-Abegg's profitability is expected to be in line with that of its own operations in the area within three years after closing of the transaction, which is anticipated in the second half of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.

ABB said it intends to retain Ziehl-Abegg's headquarters in Kuenzelsau, Germany, and that it will remain committed to the country.

data.title: ConocoPhillips announces agreement to sell Norway business and Teesside asset to Vår Energi
data.description:
ConocoPhillips announces agreement to sell Norway business and Teesside asset to Vår Energi

ConocoPhillips (NYSE: COP) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Norway business and its 40.25% interest in and operatorship of the U.K. Teesside oil terminal to Vår Energi for total consideration of $4.425 billion, less agreed upon adjustments of approximately $0.5 billion as of the Jan. 1, 2026, effective date. The transaction is expected to close by the end of the first quarter 2027 subject to approval by the Norwegian Ministry of Energy and regulatory conditions.

At closing, Vår Energi will assume the post-effective date balance sheets of the properties. Total consideration is expected to be $3.9 billion, including the remaining 2026 tax liability of approximately $1.4 billion, payable in the first half of 2027, and net cash proceeds of approximately $2.5 billion. Proceeds will be earmarked for general purposes and for discretionary share repurchases in 2027 to supplement the company’s long-standing commitment of returning approximately 45% of cash from operations to shareholders.

“We are extremely proud of the legacy we created with these assets for more than five decades and are pleased that Vår Energi recognizes the value of this business,” said Andy O’Brien, president and chief executive officer. “Norway and Teesside are high-quality assets with strong operating histories, and we believe this win-win transaction unlocks value for ConocoPhillips while positioning these assets for continued success under new ownership.”

The transaction includes the entire issued share capital of ConocoPhillips Skandinavia AS and ConocoPhillips (U.K.) Teesside Operator Limited, which together hold the company's Norway and Teesside assets and associated decommissioning liabilities.

The Norway business includes ConocoPhillips' interests in producing assets on the Norwegian continental shelf, anchored by the operated Greater Ekofisk Area in the North Sea, as well as interests in eight partner-operated fields across the Norwegian Sea and northern North Sea. It also includes the company's interest in the Norpipe oil pipeline and certain non-operated infrastructure. The Teesside business includes the Teesside oil terminal and related pipeline infrastructure.

In 2025, the Norway business produced approximately 120 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. Year-end 2025 proved reserves associated with the sale properties were approximately 221 million barrels of oil equivalent.

--- # # # ---

About ConocoPhillips

ConocoPhillips is a global exploration and production company with a deep, durable and diverse portfolio of oil and natural gas assets and a compelling pipeline of organic growth opportunities. We safely and responsibly develop the energy resources the world needs while delivering competitive returns to shareholders through the cycles. Our disciplined, returns-focused strategy is designed to create long-term value and position ConocoPhillips to thrive across a range of market conditions. Learn more at www.conocophillips.com.

data.title: Bureau Veritas Acquires Topo Solutions to Enhance Its AI-Powered Supply Chain Intelligence Offering
data.description:
Bureau Veritas Acquires Topo Solutions to Enhance Its AI-Powered Supply Chain Intelligence Offering

Bureau Veritas, a global leader in Testing, Inspection, and Certification services (TIC), announces the acquisition of Topo Solutions, an AI-enabled, digital end-to-end supply chain management platform. Consistent with the LEAP | 28 strategic objectives, this acquisition enables Bureau Veritas to bring a new generation of data-driven services and digital solutions to consumer goods companies and retailers around the world.

Headquartered in Hong Kong, Topo Solutions connects brands and retailers with their suppliers, factories and service providers across multiple markets worldwide by providing insight into their end-to-end supply chain in a single platform. Topo Solutions’ offering covers the entire product lifecycle, from sourcing and product development to production, quality, compliance, sustainability and shipping. In 2025, the company generated c. €3 million in revenue.

Through cloud-based collaboration, AI-powered workflow automation and advanced analytics, Topo Solutions enables customers to streamline processes, improve supply chain visibility and make faster, data-driven decisions. Topo Solutions has developed a robust platform that is actively utilized by multiple, world-class partners, offering differentiated analytics and visualization features.

“This move perfectly illustrates our LEAP | 28 strategy to accelerate growth in strategic markets through bolt-on acquisitions,” said Hinda Gharbi, Chief Executive Officer of Bureau Veritas. “Together, Bureau Veritas and Topo Solutions will turn data into actionable intelligence, helping customers make smarter decisions, strengthen supply chain resilience and sustainability, and reduce risks and costs. A warm welcome to our Topo colleagues at Bureau Veritas.”

ABOUT BUREAU VERITAS

Bureau Veritas is a world leader in inspection, certification, and laboratory testing services with a powerful purpose: to shape a world of trust by ensuring responsible progress. With a vision to be the preferred partner for customers’ excellence and sustainability, the Company innovates to help them navigate change.

Created in 1828, Bureau Veritas’ 82,000 employees deliver services in 140 countries. The Company’s technical experts support customers to address challenges in quality, health and safety, environmental protection, and sustainability.

Bureau Veritas is listed on Euronext Paris and belongs to the CAC 40, CAC 40 ESG, SBF 120 indices and is part of the CAC SBT 1.5° index. Compartment A, ISIN code FR 0006174348, stock symbol: BVI.

data.title: Maybank Profit Climbs on Stronger Fee Income, Beating Estimates — Update
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

Malayan Banking posted stronger-than-expected net profit in the third quarter, driven by higher core fee income and net fund-based income.

Malaysia's largest lender by market capitalization said Monday that quarterly net profit rose 4.7% from a year earlier to 2.74 billion ringgit, equivalent to $666.2 million. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha had expected 2.71 billion ringgit.

A 7.7% increase in core fees, led by higher wealth-management and investment banking-related income, supported the bottom line, Maybank said. Net fund-based income also grew, rising 2.3% to 5.12 billion ringgit as net interest margin improved five basis points to 2.07%.

However, net interest income--the difference between interest earned on loans and that paid on deposits--slipped 4.3% to 3.13 billion ringgit, and noninterest income fell 3.2% to 2.38 billion ringgit, it said.

Net impairment provisions for the quarter declined 39% to 215.2 million ringgit.

Maybank Chief Executive Khairussaleh Ramli said that while its diversified businesses and regional operations supported performance, the group remains cautious about the outlook amid global economic challenges and geopolitical uncertainty.

Shares of the Malaysian lender have declined nearly 5% this year, pressured by concerns about funding costs and net interest margins as bond yields rise amid a more hawkish Federal Reserve outlook.

The planned expansion of the Kuala Lumpur Composite Index to 50 constituents from 30, aimed at reducing the index's concentration in financial stocks, has also weighed on sentiment toward the bank, an index heavyweight.

Analysts said a potential rate hike by Malaysia's central bank next March could offer Malaysian banks some respite. Banks' net interest margins have been squeezed as U.S. Treasury yields lift domestic bond yields and funding costs and intense deposit competition pushes lenders to offer higher rates.

A 25-basis-point increase in Bank Negara Malaysia's policy rate could improve Maybank's net interest margin by 2.6 basis points, according to estimates by CIMB Securities, which is overweight on the Malaysia banking sector.

That relief would likely be temporary, however. The potential rate increase is a short-term positive catalyst for banks' margins rather than a structural solution to the sector's funding challenges, CIMB Securities analyst Ei Leen Tan said.

data.title: Partners Group to Buy New Zealand Transport Firm From Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners
data.description:
By Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Private-markets firm Partners Group has agreed to acquire a New Zealand transport firm from Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners amid rising client demand for income-oriented infrastructure assets.

Partners Group, which oversees more than $186 billion in assets, said it will invest in StraitNZ from select pools of capital and plans to work with management to further grow the company's recurring revenue base.

No financial terms were disclosed.

StraitNZ is an integrated transport, logistics and ferry company managing freight and passenger services across the Cook Strait. It is one of two ferry operators connecting New Zealand's national highway system from the North Island to the South Island.

Nicholas Kuys, managing director for infrastructure at Partners Group, said the company holds a defensive position on the transport route that's a backbone of the New Zealand economy.

Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners said that since it invested in the company in March 2022, StraitNZ has delivered strong growth in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.

The deal is in line with Partners Group's expectations that the trend of client demand for strategic brownfield investments will accelerate as more investors recognize the benefits of exposure to such assets.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals and other conditions.
